newsitem.title: USA: California bill seeks to treat chronic gamblers.
newsitem.headline: California bill seeks to treat chronic gamblers.

text.p: "Pathological" gamblers would be able to get help under a measure proposed by a California legislator Thursday.

California Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, said he would add the provision to his bill, already before the state legislature, which would create a state entity to regulate gambling in California.
Lockyer said he would propose setting up a toll-free hotline number for gamblers to call for help with gambling addictions. The cost would be shared by gaming organizations.
He also called for a "pathological gambling program" at the Department of Alcohol and Drug Abuse "to take the lead in problem gambling and research and provide counseling assistance."
He also called for an education program to combat underage gambling.

"The problems with gambling aren't limited to regulation," Lockyer said in a statement. "The social costs of gambling addiction for California number in the billions of dollars and there needs to be treatment programs and help-lines."

According to a state report released Thursday, there are about 400,000 pathological gamblers in the state. The report by the California Research Bureau estimated the social cost of gambling in the state at $5 billion a year.
The bureau said Californians wager about $14.6 billion annually. The state ranks sixth in the nation in terms of gambling dollars wagered.

Many forms of gambling are illegal in California, but state residents can legally bet on horse racing, and can gamble through the state lottery, card clubs and bingo parlors. Indian tribes have also set up casinos on reservations in the state.
